findings.reason: I confirmed that one try wraps the whole loop and that the Prisma delete promises are lazy and only run at the Promise.all, so a single SendGrid failure stops the remaining cancels and leaves every row in place, and the next cron run retries them in the same order.

This is phrased as a question, but it is a plausible concern: the workflow-delete, step-delete and reschedule paths still POST cancel to SendGrid immediately, once per reminder, without awaiting, and a failed cancel is only logged.

I confirmed that the old code awaited the deleteMany calls in prismaPromises, and that the new code calls the async helpers fire-and-forget inside forEach, so the cancelled flag update or row delete may never finish before the handler returns.
This is correct: the async helpers catch their own errors and their promises are dropped inside forEach, so the outer catch can never fire; it is dead code, not a behaviour defect.

I confirmed that the SMS helper deletes the row without being awaited while workflow.deleteMany cascades the same row, so whichever runs second fails and writes a misleading error log; nothing is lost.
I confirmed that Prisma is imported but unused and that PrismaPromise is only used as a type after the import was changed to a value import; this is import hygiene and comment reformatting only.
